script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Workplace
Theme: friendship

Begin screenplay.

Title: The Unseen

INT. BUREAU - DAY

JESS (30s, dressed in business attire) enters the bureau, a large, open-plan office filled with workstations. The employees look up from their desks as she arrives.

JESS (V.O.)
(internal monologue)
The clock struck eight. The morning rush of arriving employees had slowed to a trickle. My workplace, the Bureau, was a cacophony of keyboards tapping, phones ringing, and hushed conversations. Yet, beneath this facade of productivity, there was another world - The Unseen.

INT. JESS' OFFICE - DAY

Jess sits at her desk, shuffling papers and glancing at the clock. Her computer screen displays a photograph of her and her two friends, EMMA (early 30s, with short, curly hair) and MIKE (late 30s, with a shaved head).

Jess' phone buzzes, and she looks up, expecting an important call. Instead, it's a text message from Emma.

EMMA (V.O.) (TEXT)
Hey Jess, do you want to grab lunch today?

INT. BUREAU CAFETERIA - DAY

Jess walks into the crowded cafeteria, passing by employees eating at long tables. She spots Emma and Mike at their usual table, sitting and laughing. Jess takes a seat between them.

EMMA
Hey there, sunshine! You're late today.

MIKE
Yeah, we were starting to worry about you.

JESS
Sorry, I got caught up in a project.

They continue laughing and chatting as they eat their lunch, their friendship a bright spot in the otherwise monotonous workday.

INT. JESS' OFFICE - DAY

Jess sits at her desk, her thoughts drifting to her friends. She looks at a drawing of a family that she keeps on her desk – a reminder of the life she wants to build with them.

Jess' phone buzzes, snapping her back to reality. It's an email from her boss. She reads it, her expression growing serious.

INT. BUREAU - DAY

Jess walks through the office, her friends calling out to her as she passes. She stops by her boss' office and enters.

BOSS (50s, stern expression) looks up from his papers as she enters.

BOSS
Ah, Jess, come in. I've got some news for you.

Jess' heart races as she braces herself for the worst.

BOSS
We've been asked to take on a new project, and I think you'd be perfect for it. It's a big opportunity, and I want you to lead the team.

Jess is taken aback by the news, her initial worry replaced by excitement.

JESS
Thank you, sir. I won't let you down.

INT. BUREAU CAFETERIA - DAY

Emma and Mike congratulate Jess on her new role, their pride in her obvious. They celebrate with a round of mocktails, laughing and toasting to her success.

INT. JESS' OFFICE - NIGHT

Jess sits at her desk, the office now deserted. She looks at the photograph of her friends and smiles, her thoughts filled with gratitude for their support.

Jess' phone buzzes again, this time with a group text from Emma and Mike.

EMMA (V.O.) (TEXT)
Hey Jess, we're going out for dinner tonight. Come join us.

Jess looks up, her smile growing wider.

JESS (V.O.)
The Unseen, my friends, were always there, supporting me, lifting me up, and reminding me of what truly matters in life.

FADE OUT.

END OF SCREENPLAY.
